scope: Exact classical inputs for S_n and C_m realization over Q. No novelty claim and no general inverse Galois solution.
authentication: Official author-hosted PDFs were opened with web tools; relevant pages were inspected by PDF screenshot and source text. Local copies were hashed and text extracted. Full PDFs remain private and are not for distribution.

results.locator: Theorem 4.28, printed p. 69, zero-based PDF index 78
results.paraphrase: For monic f in Z[X], a prime p with squarefree reduction yields a Galois permutation whose cycle lengths are the degrees of the distinct irreducible reduction factors.
A transitive subgroup of S_n containing a transposition and an (n−1)-cycle is S_n.
CRT combines reduction patterns n; 1+(n−1); and 2 plus odd degrees to realize S_n over Q.
results.status: proved construction with monicity caveat below

results.paraphrase: Finite fields of every prime power order exist and their extensions are simple.
For finite Galois E/F and normal H, E^H/F is Galois with group Gal(E/F)/H.
An irreducible polynomial over Q of prime degree p with exactly two nonreal roots has Galois group S_p.
results.status: proved; prime degree is essential to this criterion

results.paraphrase: Every finite subgroup of a field’s multiplicative group is cyclic.
When char(K) does not divide N, exponent action on Nth roots embeds Gal(K(mu_N)/K) into (Z/NZ)^×.
For every positive N, the exponent map Gal(Q(mu_N)/Q) to (Z/NZ)^× is an isomorphism.
If p does not divide N, reduction of Phi_N modulo p has distinct irreducible factors, each of degree ord_N(p).
For coprime integers a and m with m positive, infinitely many numbers a+mn, with n positive, are prime.
results.status: stated classical Dirichlet theorem; proof not included in these notes

notation_dictionary.mu_N: Set/group of all Nth roots of unity in an algebraic closure; Q(mu_N)=Q(zeta_N)
notation_dictionary.zeta_N: A chosen primitive Nth root of unity
notation_dictionary.G_f: Gal(E_f/Q), where E_f is the splitting field of f over Q
notation_dictionary.Gal(Q(zeta_p)/Q): Cyclic order p−1 via the exponent identification with F_p^×
notation_dictionary.m: Target cyclic group order; independent of cyclotomic conductor p

application.symmetric: For n>=3 use squarefree reduction patterns and monic coefficientwise CRT. For n=1 use Q/Q, and for n=2 use X^2−2. Degree n does not mean extension degree n: an S_n splitting field has degree n!.
application.cyclic: For m>1, Dirichlet with a=1 gives a prime p congruent to 1 modulo m. Let E=Q(zeta_p), and let H be its unique subgroup of order (p−1)/m. Then L=E^H is Galois over Q with group C_m. For m=1 use Q.
application.optional_dirichlet_free_route: For m>1, Phi_m has constant term 1 and |Phi_m(m)|>1 by its complex root product. Any prime p dividing Phi_m(m) does not divide m. The linear root m modulo p and Conrad Theorem 5.4 imply ord_m(p)=1, so p is congruent to 1 modulo m. This supplies the prime needed for the same fixed-field construction without invoking full Dirichlet.
application.optional_explicit_generator: A Gaussian period eta=sum_{h in H} zeta_p^h has stabilizer H. Distinct coset sums differ by a nonzero linear combination of zeta_p,...,zeta_p^(p−1), which are Q-linearly independent. Thus Q(eta)=E^H. This is a formal classical corollary, not a novelty claim.

caveats: Milne Example 4.32 prints f=15f_1+10f_2+6f_3 for monic degree-n f_i. That expression has leading coefficient 31. Subtract 30X^n to preserve all three residues and ensure monicity, or use coefficientwise monic CRT. This addresses the monic hypothesis of Theorem 4.28.
All irreducible finite-field factors used in the CRT construction must be separable; avoid repeated linear factors in low-degree edge cases.
Conrad’s arbitrary-base cyclotomic embedding can be proper. The full unit group identification used here is specifically over Q.
The cyclic field L is generally a subfield of Q(zeta_p), not Q(zeta_m). Its degree m follows from a quotient, not from imposing phi(m)=m.
An arbitrary subgroup G of S_n gives E/E^G with group G. Its base E^G is generally a number field larger than Q. This is not the rational inverse Galois conclusion.
This bounded check authenticates classical source inputs. It does not establish current global open-problem status or survey all realization theorems.
